info.title: Microworker API
info.description:
Post and fund tasks, track automatic payments and reject submissions from your own server.

Authenticate with an API key from https://microworker.app/developers/ — send it as `Authorization: Bearer mwk_…` (or `X-API-Key`). Keys are for servers: never put one in a web page or an app.

A key has scopes: `read` (always), `tasks` (create and edit tasks; pause, resume, cancel, edit, slow down and post notes on live ones), `fund` (publish using your balance, and change a live task's places and pay), `review` (reject submissions only) and `conversions` (confirm sign-ups for automatic payment on postback tasks). Employers cannot manually approve submissions. Existing Review keys need a new key with `conversions` to confirm sign-ups.

Money is in integer cents (`*_minor`). The platform fee is 5% plus $1.00 per task; verified employers pay no fee. Rewards start at $0.02 per worker ($0.05 when the task asks for a screenshot or a file). Current figures are always on GET https://microworker.app/api/version.

Limits: 120 requests a minute per key, 30 of them for funding (a create with `fund: true` too), changing a live task's places and pay, rejection and conversion confirmations; and 3000 writes an hour per key (10000 an hour from one network address, whatever the key — GET /me `limits`). Errors are `{ "error": "<code>" }` with an HTTP status.

Webhooks: add an https endpoint and we POST signed events to it — see the webhooks section and the WebhookEvent schema. Conversion postbacks: post a task with verify_method "postback" and confirm each real sign-up with POST /conversions — it pays at once; check it later and ask for a fix (POST /submissions/{id}/revise) or take the pay back (POST /submissions/{id}/reverse).

post.summary: Recommend a reward per worker
post.description: What similar work pays, from the posting itself: what it asks for (tests, surveys, data work, short videos, sign-ups, installs, social media actions…), how many steps and proofs it has, a duration it states, where workers must be, the devices they must be on, and whether it is only for your own workers. Screenshot and file proofs include estimated capture/upload handling, even for the first proof and on duration-based recommendations; text, URLs and copied codes have no media handling premium. Every factor comes back in `reasons`. A recommendation only — you set the price, from the floor (`floor_minor`) up. The same guide is on the website's Post a task page.

post.summary: Create a task (as a draft), or create and fund it
post.description:
Creates a DRAFT: nothing is charged and no worker can see it until you fund it. `fee_minor` in the answer is a preview; the fee actually charged is worked out again when you fund. With `x_check: true` each worker's X work is checked automatically and `fee_minor` includes the charge for it (`x_check_fee_minor`): 503 `x_check_unavailable` when X checks are off (GET /version `verification.x_check`), 422 `x_check_no_target` when the task names nothing on X a check can see, 422 `x_check_not_for_postback` on a conversion task.

The job minimum is `min_task_budget_minor` on GET /version ($1.00): reward × workers must reach it, or 400 `budget_below_minimum` with `min_minor`. An account that pays no fee (a live Verified plan) has `min_task_budget_fee_free_minor` instead (0 — only the reward floor applies), so post at the size you need; if the plan has lapsed the answer is 400 `budget_below_minimum` with `min_minor`.

`fund: true` creates AND funds in one call: the draft goes straight through POST /tasks/{id}/fund — the same checks, review and money. Needs the `fund` scope as well, and counts toward the money limit. Funded: 201 with the task, `funded: true` and the funding's fields (`escrow_minor`, `under_review`…). Refused: the funding's own status and code, with `funded: false`, `task_id` and the created task as `task` — it stays a draft you can fund, change or cancel.

`dedupe_keys` and `order_ref`: see TaskCreate.

get.summary: One of your tasks, with submission counts
get.description: The whole task (instructions, proof requirements, targeting and attachments, and once it is live your `notes` and when its words last changed, `edited_at`) and how many of its submissions are in each state; `approved` includes automatic approvals. Why it is filling or not: `counts.free_places` (what a new worker can still take — an open dispute and a proof waiting for a place each keep one back), `counts.in_progress`, `counts.held`, `counts.disputes_open`, `visibility` (whether workers see it on the board now, and why not) and `board_kind` (where the board lists it). patch.summary: Edit a draft, or pause / resume / cancel a task
patch.description:
Field edits are accepted while the task is a draft; on a live task they answer 409 `invalid_task_state` — its words, notes, places and pay have calls of their own (the Live tasks section).

On a live task send only `action` (other fields sent with it are ignored):
- `pause` — an open task leaves the board and nobody new can start it. Workers who already started can still send their proof.
- `unpause` — resume a paused task. It goes through the funding checks again first: 422 `task_link_broken` (with `url`, `kind` and `detail`) when a link no longer works, 422 `task_other_platform` (with `names`) or `task_material_missing` (with `material`) when a worker here could not do it — fix it with POST /tasks/{id}/edit, then resume. 409 `task_under_review` while staff hold it.
- `cancel` — end a draft, open or paused task and return its unspent budget to your balance. Refused with 409 `cannot_cancel_with_pending_submissions` while proof waits for its review. An open dispute keeps back only what it would pay (`dispute_reserve_minor` in the answer): each decision pays the worker from it or refunds it to you. (`cannot_cancel_with_open_disputes` only while that reserve is switched off.)

refunded_minor.description: On cancel: what came back to your balance.

match_credit_returned_minor.description: On cancel, when switch-offer match credit was left in the task: it goes back to your offer, not your balance.

dispute_reserve_minor.description: On cancel with open disputes: what stays in the task to pay them if they are decided for the worker; the rest comes back to you as each one is decided.

post.summary: Fund a draft and publish it
post.description: Reserves reward × workers + the platform fee from your available balance as the task's budget and publishes the task. The posting is screened first: a refusal is a 422 `content_policy_violation` and no money moves. Some kinds of task (gambling, software downloads, and categories with a `min_plan`) need a live plan: without one the answer is a 403 `verified_required` with `category` and `plan`, and the task stays a draft. A task for `my_workers` answers 409 `team_empty` while you have saved no worker, and a task for a project's team (`audience: "project"`) while its project has nobody in it; nothing is charged. A team-first task opens to everyone `backup_hours` after funding (`open_to_all_at`). A `max_per_country` at or above the worker count being funded is cleared, since it would limit nothing. A first task, or one the screen flags, may publish with `under_review: true`. When our AI reviewer refuses a posting a person may still approve, an account without a plan gets a 403 `verified_required` with `review: true` and the reviewer's `reason`; with a plan it is funded and held for a person (`under_review: true`, `review: "person"`) until our team approves it or declines it (the budget comes back to your balance). A task with `x_check` also reserves the X-check charge for every place, at today's price (frozen on the task; never waived by a plan): 503 `x_check_unavailable` when X checks are off, 422 `x_check_no_target` when the draft no longer names anything on X. A task with `personal_links` needs one for every place: 409 `personal_links_short` with `needed`, and nothing is charged. Needs the `fund` scope.

get.summary: Submissions on one of your tasks
get.description:
Each carries the automatic checks' verdict: `check_status` is `clear`, `warn` or `hold` (held proof is excluded from automatic payment), and `check_flags` says what was found. The `approved` filter includes automatic approvals; `auto_approved` selects only automatic approvals. Screenshot paths are fetched with GET /proofs/{file}. `worker_ref` is the worker's id for your account — what `{worker}` in your steps showed them.

With none of `since_id`, `updated_since`, `limit` or `cursor` the answer is every row, newest first, as it always was. With any of them it is a page: `since_id` returns submissions made after that id, oldest first; `updated_since` returns those that CHANGED at or after that time (a new status, a proof, a check), oldest change first — poll with the time of your last call; `limit` (1–500, default 100) sizes the page; `next_cursor` is null on the last page, else pass it as `cursor` (alone, or with `status`) for the next. Each paged row carries its `updated_at`. A malformed value answers 400 `validation_failed` with `field`.

parameters.description: Only submissions that changed at or after this time (ISO 8601 — a zone or Z; without one it is UTC), oldest change first.

get.summary: Submissions on all your tasks, one feed
get.description:
The rows of GET /tasks/{id}/submissions — the same fields, `task_id` on each — across every task of yours, so one call replaces one per task. Always paged, as that call is with paging: `updated_since` (what CHANGED at or after that time — poll with the time of your last call), `since_id` (what is new after that id), `limit` (1–500, default 100), and `next_cursor` (null on the last page) passed back as `cursor`. With none of them it starts from your first submission. Narrow it with `status`, `task_id` or `order_ref`. Each row carries its `updated_at`.

Webhooks push the same news to you as it happens (`submission.created`, `submission.approved`…): poll this when you want to be sure you missed nothing.

post.summary: Reject a submission
post.description: Say why — the worker sees `rejection_reason`. A FIX FIRST (since 2026-11-02): your first refusal of a proof that was never sent back for a fix is a fix request — the proof goes back to its worker with your reason and a few hours to send it again (the answer says `sent_back: true`, `status: "claimed"` and `fix`), and they keep their place meanwhile; when they send it again you get `submission.created` for the same submission and decide again, and only a refusal of the fixed proof is final. Send `final: true` to refuse at once (a proof that is not the worker's own work). A final refusal moves no money and the slot goes back to the pool for another worker. A conversion task, a task paid with free credit and a task that is no longer live are always refused at once.

status.description: With `sent_back`: the proof is the worker's again until they send the fix.

post.summary: Approve a submission and pay it
post.description: On your own task with `employer_review: true`: pay a PENDING proof you have checked — the worker is paid at once, a proof held for a person included. On a task without it every proof is decided by our automatic review (403 `automatic_approval_only`); a held one there is cleared with POST /submissions/{id}/release. While the automatic checks on a proof are still running the answer is 409 `checks_pending` — ask again in a minute. Not on a task paid with free credit (409 `credit_job_review`: our team decides those) nor on a conversion task (409 `submission_not_approvable`: POST /conversions confirms those). When an open dispute on the task holds its money, the approval is recorded and the worker is paid as soon as the dispute is decided (`paid: false`, `queued: true`).

post.summary: Release a held submission
post.description: For a PENDING proof on your own task that our automatic checks or review HELD for a person (`check_status` `hold`, or `review_state` `held`): you looked, and it is fine. It is paid within a minute by our review — this call moves no money itself, and the proof can still be rejected until it is paid. The same as the Release button on your job page. Not on a task paid with free credit (409 `credit_job_review`: our team decides those).

post.summary: Ask the worker to fix their work
post.description:
On your own task with `employer_review: true`: send a PENDING proof back to its worker with your note (shown as written) and a time to send it again (`hours`, 1–24, the default; more is cut to it). Nothing is paid; the place stays theirs, and the proof comes back as pending for you to decide. At most 2 fixes per proof (409 `fix_limit_reached`); `revisions_left` says how many remain. On a task without employer review our automatic review asks for fixes itself (409 `submission_not_revisable`), and on a task paid with free credit our team decides (409 `credit_job_review`).

On your own conversion (postback) task: send the work back with a note the worker reads as written, and a time to fix it (`hours`, 1–24, the default; more is cut to it). Their personal link keeps working. On work not paid yet (claimed, or "I've finished") nothing is paid until you confirm it with POST /conversions. On PAID work (up to 30 days after it was paid) the pay stays — confirm it again with the same click before `fix.due_at` and it is kept, or it is taken back automatically as not done, with your note as the reason. At most 2 fix requests per submission; a new one replaces an open one.

If the worker's earned balance cannot cover it, the rest is kept from their next pay. The worker can dispute it, and a person decides; if they side with the worker the pay is restored. Once per submission.

post.summary: Report paid proof work to our staff
post.description: On your own PROOF task (conversion tasks use POST /submissions/{id}/reverse), for work our review paid, up to 30 days after it was paid: your later check found it not done — the answers were left blank, the screenshot was of another survey. We look at the proof again at once, with your reason beside it: when two looks agree the work was not done, the pay is taken back (no fine for the worker; it comes back to the task, with the place reopened, while the task is live, else to your balance) and the worker may dispute that to our staff. Anything the check cannot settle waits for our staff, who take the pay back, confirm it a fake, or keep it paid. You are told the outcome. The `reason` (10–1000 characters) is for our staff. Once per submission: a second report answers the first, with `already: true`.

get.description: A worker who thinks a refusal was wrong can dispute it, once per proof. On a refusal YOU made (`refusal.by` `you`) you decide first: pay the worker (POST /disputes/{id}/accept), keep your refusal (POST /disputes/{id}/uphold) or let them send it again (POST /disputes/{id}/send-back). If nobody decides by `decide_by` (48 hours after it opened), our automatic look decides. It reads your refusal's reason beside the worker's words, and does not approve over a specific reason it cannot check itself (a code you gave out, your own records, an account that already did the work). Unless it finds the work done, your refusal stands. When it does: a task with a `verify_url` is asked once more — event `dispute.check` (header `Microworker-Event`), signed like `proof.check`, body `{ "event": "dispute.check", "task_id", "submission_id", "dispute_id", "worker_ref", "proof": { "text", "url" }, "refusal": { "reason" }, "dispute": { "reason" } }`, answered within 5 seconds — and `{ "valid": false, "reason": "…" }` keeps your refusal (the worker reads your reason), `{ "valid": true }` pays the worker. With no clear answer (or no `verify_url`), a refusal you gave a reason for is not paid: it waits for our staff (`waiting_for` `staff`, `staff_review`), and your refusal stands by itself at the new `decide_by` (48 hours later). You can still decide it yourself meanwhile. A refusal without a reason is paid. A refusal our automatic review made (`automatic`) is decided by that look within moments — when it finds only something missing, it lets the worker send it again by itself (`sent_back`); you may still pay it or send it back; one our staff made (`staff`) is decided by our staff. `can_accept`, `can_uphold` and `can_send_back` say what you can do now. `automatic_look` is what our look found (advice until the time runs out). Open disputes by default; `status=all` includes decided ones. The webhooks `dispute.opened` and `dispute.decided` carry the same object.

post.summary: Change a live task's words
post.description:
Change the title, the steps, each proof requirement's note and which step each attachment belongs to, on an open or paused task. Send only what changes; the answer is the task as it now is.

The KINDS of proof and their number stay as they are — a worker may be half way through sending exactly those — so `proof_notes` has one entry per requirement, in order. Money and who can take the task do not change here: places and pay are POST /tasks/{id}/resize.

The new words are checked the way funding checks them: the content rules, kinds of task only a plan may post, the links the edit adds, whether a worker here can do it, and — for words the screen flags — the reviewer. A refusal changes nothing. `dry_run: true` runs every check and changes nothing: try first.

When the words change, the version before is kept, and the people working on the task (a claim still open, or proof sent back for a fix) are told. `message` is what they are told; it is also posted as a note. Proof already sent is judged against the version its worker started with.

`checker_note` — your private note for checking proofs — changes with the words or alone. Alone it tells nobody, keeps no version and leaves `edited_at` as it was: workers never see it. It is screened by the content rules at once (422 `content_policy_violation` with `field: "checker_note"`).

post.summary: Change a live task's places and pay
post.description:
Fewer or more places (`slots_total`) and higher pay (`reward_minor`) on an open or paused task. Pay can only go up. Places cannot go below the places in use (started, waiting for review or paid) plus one for each open dispute (the place it is paid from if it is decided for the worker), and one place must stay unpaid.

Only the difference moves: fewer places or a smaller fee bring money back to your available balance (`refund_minor`); more places or higher pay reserve it from your balance as part of the task's budget (`extra_minor` — 402 `insufficient_balance` when it is not there, `earnings_cannot_fund` when only money you earned is: a raise is paid with money you added). Workers who started get the new pay; proof already sent keeps the price it was sent at. The fee is worked out again on the new budget at your terms now (verified employers pay none).

`dry_run: true` answers the same thing and changes nothing. Needs the `fund` scope, and counts toward the money limit — dry runs too.

A task with groups of workers (`variations`): change each group's places and pay with `variations`; each group is planned like the task, at its own pay, and the task's numbers are the sums.

post.summary: Stop a task and let the people on it finish
post.description:
The way to stop a task without closing the work of the people already on it (a cancel closes every start not sent yet, unpaid). An open or paused task is paused — nobody new starts it — and its places come down to the ones in use (started, waiting for a decision, paid, one per open dispute), the free places' money back to your balance now (`refund_minor`). The people on it send their proof and are paid as usual; the task completes when the last place is paid. A task with groups of workers (`variations`) is only paused.

With nobody working on it, it is cancelled the usual way (`status: "cancelled"`) — refused like a cancel while a proof waits for your decision (409 `cannot_cancel_with_pending_submissions`) or a proof is out for a fix (409 `cannot_cancel_with_fixes`). It only gives money back, so it needs the `tasks` scope and does not count toward the money limit.

patch.description: Send any of `events`, `url` and `active`; the secret stays the same. `events`: the events it gets from now on (the names of POST /webhooks; at least one — 400 `events_invalid` for an empty list, `validation_failed` for a name we do not send). `url`: the same checks as a new endpoint (400 `url_not_https`, `url_not_public`, `url_invalid`, `url_port`); deliveries still waiting go to the new address. `active: false` switches it off (`disabled_reason: "paused"`) — nothing is queued for it while it is off, and what was already waiting is sent once it is back on; `active: true` switches it on again, also one switched off after 50 failures in a row (its failure count starts over), while you have fewer than five endpoints on (409 `too_many_webhooks`). Answers the endpoint. An endpoint that is not yours answers 404 `webhook_not_found`.

post.summary: Confirm a conversion (pays the worker)
post.description: For a task posted with `verify_method: "postback"`. Each worker who claims it gets a personal link — your `verify_target` with `mw_click=<code>` added. Store that code when they sign up; when the sign-up is real, send it here and the worker is paid on the spot — after our account checks (one phone is one person): `status: "held"` means they held it for a person to decide, `checking: true` that they are still running and the payment follows them (webhook `submission.approved`). A worker's "I've finished" you neither confirm nor reject within 3 days is closed without pay. Needs the `conversions` scope.

apiKey.description: An API key from /developers, as `Authorization: Bearer mwk_…`.

apiKeyHeader.name: X-API-Key
apiKeyHeader.description: The same API key, sent as `X-API-Key: mwk_…` instead of the Bearer header.

write_per_hour.description: Writes (creating, funding, editing, approving, rejecting…) this key may make in an hour.

min_plan.description: The plan a task in this category needs before it can be funded; null for any account.

must_show.description: Screenshot rows only: text the screenshot must show (a group or channel name, a username). We read each screenshot on our own server and hold a submission that does not show it.

type.description: `code`: a completion code you show at the end of your own flow; a matching code pays on the spot. At most one per task.

note.description: What the proof must show. Workers are judged against it.

answer.description: For `code` only: the code (5–64 letters or digits). Stored hashed and never returned; on an edit, omit it to keep the stored one.

TargetProfile.description: Who can do this (2026-10-07): only workers whose Skills & assets match see the task and can claim it (others get 403 `profile_not_matching`). Within a part ANY choice will do; every part given must be met. null or every part empty = anybody. Each part given raises the price guide ×1.2, at most ×2.

wants.description: The kinds of work they asked for.

channel.description: Runs a page or channel of at least `min_followers` (a band), on one of `platforms` (empty = any).

instructions.description: The steps, one per line. `**bold**` and `*italic*` render; nothing else does.

reward_minor.description: Pay per approved worker, in cents. The floor is `min_reward_minor` on /version, or `min_reward_screenshot_minor` when the task asks for a screenshot or a file.

auto_approve_hours.description: Defaults to 0 when omitted, and is never more than 24: a larger value is accepted and stored as 24. Proof is paid as soon as the automatic checks are clear; anything they question is paid within 24 h unless you reject it first (sooner when this window is shorter); held proofs wait for a person. 0 = instant review. GET /version `payment` has the current figures.

target_countries.description: Only workers in these countries. Empty = anywhere.

target_devices.description: Only workers on these devices — the device they open and claim the task on. `windows` and `mac` are computers running that system (`desktop` is any computer). Empty, or android + ios + a computer, = any device.

audience.description: `my_workers`: only the workers you saved from your own tasks' review page can see and claim it (funding answers 409 `team_empty` until you have saved one). `project`: your project's team first (needs `project_id`; 400 `project_required` without one), then everyone after `backup_hours`.

hiring.description: A test task: you are choosing workers from it for more work. Workers see it on the task.

project_id.description: One of your projects (not archived; 404 `project_not_found` otherwise). The task is listed on the project; with `audience: "project"` its team gets it first.

backup_hours.description: For `audience: "project"`: hours after funding before the spots the team has not taken open to everyone. 0 = never.

max_per_country.description: At most this many of the workers from any one country — counted by the country each worker connects from when they start the task. null (or omitted) = no limit; a value at or above `slots_total` limits nothing and is stored as null. A worker whose country's places are all taken is refused with 403 `country_quota_full`.

verify_method.description: `telegram_join`: the platform checks the join itself. `postback`: your server confirms each conversion with POST /conversions, and that pays the worker.

verify_target.description: Required with verify_method. For telegram_join the group or channel (@mygroup); for postback the https landing URL each worker starts from.

x_check.description: Check each worker's X work automatically: that the X account in their proof follows the account your steps link to, and reposted, replied to or quoted the post they link to (likes cannot be checked — X keeps them private). A task asking only for follows and reposts is paid on X's answer; otherwise the answer is given to our proof reviewer, and work X shows not done is sent back for a fix. Costs `x_check.price_per_worker_micro` (GET /version, micro-dollars) per worker place, rounded up to the cent, added to the fee — never waived by a plan. Not on conversion (postback) tasks.

variations.description: Groups of workers doing different mixes of the task (2–6) — e.g. 20 places: 15 "Survey", 5 "Survey + 3 extra questions". Every group says how many places it has — `places`, adding up to `slots_total` (400 `variations_places_mismatch` with `places_total` and `slots_total`), or `share_percent` of `slots_total`, adding up to 100 (400 `variations_share_invalid` with `share_total`; 400 `variations_too_few_places` with `min_slots` when a share gets no place) — all the same way (400 `variations_mixed`), with names that differ (400 `variations_duplicate_label`). A group without `reward_minor` pays the task's. The budget is Σ places × pay and `reward_minor` is stored as the lowest group pay (every pay floor holds for every group). Each claim takes a place in the group furthest behind its share; workers see their group's name and line above the common steps. 503 `variations_unavailable`.

employer_review.description: You approve each proof yourself (POST /submissions/{id}/approve, or reject it) instead of our automatic review: nothing is paid by our review or by instant pay while the proof's window (`auto_approve_hours`) is open. When the window passes without your decision, our automatic review decides the proof as on any other task. For employers who can check work our review cannot — a code your own site gives each worker, an action on another platform. 503 `employer_review_unavailable`; 422 `employer_review_not_for_postback` on a conversion task, 422 `employer_review_not_for_verified` on a Telegram-join or completion-code task (the platform checks those itself). Ignored on a task paid with free credit.

dedupe_key.description: One person per item: a worker who did real work on another task of yours with this key — sent proof (waiting, paid, refused, or closed after it was sent) or holds a place on it now — cannot take this one and does not see it on the board (403 `already_did_similar` on the website). A start that ran out, or was closed, with nothing sent does not count. Use the thing being worked on — a product id, a page address. Your keys only; trimmed; matched exactly. 503 `dedupe_unavailable` when switched off.

dedupe_keys.description: Several keys (1–10): a worker who did real work on another task of yours sharing ANY of them cannot take this one (403 `already_did_similar`) and does not see it. Key each kind of work on an item on its own — a task answering survey 123 `survey:123:answer`, a task interviewing its people `survey:123:interview`, a task that may be either both — and a person who answered the survey can still be interviewed, while nobody answers it twice. `dedupe_key` is a list of one; send one or the other (both: 400 `validation_failed`, `field: "dedupe_keys"`). Trimmed, duplicates dropped, kept in your order. 503 `dedupe_unavailable` for more than one while keys are switched off.

order_ref.description: Your own name for the order this task belongs to — the same on each of its tasks (GET /orders/{ref}, and pause / resume / cancel / wind-down for all of them). Letters, digits and . _ : -; yours only, compared exactly.

fund.description: Create AND fund in one call (needs the `fund` scope; counts toward the money limit) — see POST /tasks.

verify_url.description: The submit-time check: an https address of yours we call when a worker sends proof, BEFORE it is stored — a POST with `{ event: "proof.check", task_id, submission_id, worker_ref, proof: { text, url } }` (+ `account: { platform, username }` on a task that needs a verified account), signed like a webhook (header Microworker-Signature, keyed with `verify_secret`; Microworker-Event: proof.check). It runs on every send — a re-send after a fix request too, with the same `submission_id`. Answer `{ "valid": false, "reason": "…" }` with a 2xx to turn the proof away: the worker reads your reason (contact details hidden) and can send again; nothing is stored. Anything else — `valid: true`, an error, no answer within 1500 ms — and the proof goes in as usual. The same address is asked two more questions, named in the body's `event` and the Microworker-Event header: `claim.check` when a worker starts a task posted with `verify_claims` (see that field), and `dispute.check` when a dispute of your own refusal reaches its deadline and our look found the work done — we ask once more with `{ event, task_id, submission_id, dispute_id, worker_ref, proof: { text, url }, refusal: { reason }, dispute: { reason } }`: `{ "valid": false }` keeps your refusal, `{ "valid": true }` pays it, anything else and a person decides when you gave a reason. 400 `url_not_https`, `url_not_public`, `url_invalid` or `url_port` (with `field`); 422 `verify_url_not_for_postback` on a conversion task; 503 `verify_url_unavailable`.

verify_claims.description: Ask before the start: we also call your `verify_url` the moment a worker STARTS the task, before a place is taken — a POST with `{ event: "claim.check", task_id, worker_ref, variation: { id, label } | null, attempt }` (+ `account: { platform, username }` on a task that needs a verified account) (`variation`: the group the start would take; `attempt`: 1, or 2 for a fresh start after their time ran out), signed as for proof.check (Microworker-Event: claim.check). Answer `{ "valid": false, "reason": "…" }` with a 2xx and the worker is kept off the task: no place is taken, nothing is stored, they read your reason (contact details hidden) and it does not count against them. Anything else, or no answer within 1500 ms, and the start goes on as usual — a yes is not yet a start: our own rules (places left, countries, devices…) still decide after it. A worker who already holds a place is never asked again. Needs a `verify_url` once the same request is applied (422 `verify_claims_needs_url`); not on a conversion task (422 `verify_url_not_for_postback`); 503 `verify_claims_unavailable`. Clearing `verify_url` later leaves it set but idle.

account.description: A verified account the worker must have — `{ "platform": "x" }`, `"instagram"` or `"tiktok"`. Only workers who proved such an account is theirs see and start the task (once: a short code in a public post from it — on TikTok in its bio; we read it where anybody can): the start answers 403 `account_required` `{ platform }` without one, and a worker with several picks which one the place uses. Your claim.check and proof.check, the submission webhooks and GET /submissions then name it: `account: { platform, username }`. null or absent = none. 400 `account_platform_unsupported`; 503 `accounts_unavailable`.

personal_links.description: One link per worker (for invite links that work for one person only): each worker who starts the task gets the next link nobody holds, and only they ever see it — on the task page, write one of these links in your steps where each worker's own link should appear (everybody else reads it as `{link}`). https only, each once (400 `validation_failed` with `field: "personal_links"`, `index` and `reason`), at most 500, at least as many as `slots_total` (409 `personal_links_short` with `needed`). A link a worker opened is spent for good; one given to a start that ended with nothing sent and the link never opened goes back to the list. A task with links takes each place when a worker starts it. 503 `personal_links_unavailable` when switched off.

invite_code.description: The invite code your steps ask workers to type ("Enter this invite code: ABC123") — shown on the task page in a box with Copy. One line, trimmed; null or "" = none.

checker_note.description: For checking proofs — workers never see it. What a correct proof looks like, for our automatic proof checker: a quiz's answers, the channel's @handle, which listing or address, what the finished screen shows. Read as facts about the right target and answers: it can never change our rules or choose a verdict, and the checker never repeats it to the worker. You and our staff see it with the task. Plain text, up to 2000 characters (400 `validation_failed` with `field`), trimmed; null or "" = none. Screened by our content rules when you fund (422 `content_policy_violation` with `field: "checker_note"`). 503 `checker_notes_unavailable` when switched off.

project_id.description: null takes the draft out of its project.

max_per_country.description: null clears it. Checked against the worker count the edit leaves: at or above it, it is stored as null.

x_check.description: Turn X checks on or off on a draft; `fee_minor` follows. 503 `x_check_unavailable` / 422 `x_check_no_target` as on create.

employer_review.description: Turn employer review on or off: with other edits on a draft, or sent alone on a draft, open or paused task (it moves no money; proofs already waiting keep their window). 503 / 422 as on create.

dedupe_key.description: Set, change or clear (null) the one-person-per-post key — a list of one (see `dedupe_keys`): with other edits on a draft, or sent alone (with `verify_url` or not) on a draft, open or paused task. The keys and `order_ref` sent alone are taken on a task in ANY state, a finished one too: they move no money, so you can re-key old tasks.

dedupe_keys.description: Set, change or clear (null or []) the whole list of keys, the ways `dedupe_key` is. Not with `dedupe_key` (400 `validation_failed`, `field: "dedupe_keys"`).

order_ref.description: Set, change or clear (null) the order the task belongs to: with other edits on a draft, or alone on a task in any state.

verify_url.description: Set, change or clear (null) the submit-time check, as `dedupe_key`. The answer carries `verify_secret` while one is set.

checker_note.description: Set, change or clear (null) your private note for checking proofs on a draft, with its other fields. On a live task it changes through POST /tasks/{id}/edit.

verify_claims.description: Ask before the start on or off, as `dedupe_key` (with other edits on a draft, or sent alone — with `verify_url` or not — on a draft, open or paused task). true needs a verify_url once the edit is applied (422 `verify_claims_needs_url`); 422 / 503 as on create.

account.description: The verified account a worker must have, on or off (null), as `verify_claims`: with other edits on a draft, or alone on a draft, open or paused task. Workers already on it keep their places; one without such an account is asked to prove one before sending proof (403 `account_required`).

personal_links.description: The draft's links, replaced as a whole (null or [] clears them); with other edits or alone. Every place still needs one (409 `personal_links_short` with `needed`).

invite_code.description: Set, change or clear (null) the invite code, with the draft's other fields.

variations.description: A draft's groups, replaced as a whole (as on create; with `places` and no `slots_total`, the places decide it). null takes them away: the draft keeps the places and pay the edit leaves. A new `slots_total` or `reward_minor` sent without `variations` to a draft that has groups answers 409 `variations_set`.

action.description: `pause` (open → paused), `unpause` (paused → open, once its links answer again) or `cancel` (draft, open or paused → cancelled, the unspent budget returned to your balance). Any other field sent with it is ignored.

x_check.description: Present (true) only when the task has X checks.

x_check_fee_minor.description: What the X checks add to `fee_minor` (present with `x_check`).

employer_review.description: Present (true) only when the task has employer review.

dedupe_key.description: Present when keys are set: the first of `dedupe_keys`.

funded.description: With `fund: true` only: true when the task was funded too (the funding's fields — `escrow_minor`, `under_review`… — ride along).

escrow_minor.description: With `fund: true`, once funded: what was moved into the task's budget.

under_review.description: With `fund: true`, once funded: as POST /tasks/{id}/fund answers it.

verify_secret.description: With `verify_url`: vsec_… — what signs our calls to it (the same for all your tasks). Check the signature as for webhooks.

checker_note.description: Your note for checking proofs, as stored — present when set.

verify_claims.description: Present (true) only when workers who start it are asked about first (claim.check).

account.description: Present when the task needs a verified account.

variations.description: Its groups; empty for a task without them.

personal_links.description: Its links, one per worker, in order; empty for none.

personal_link_counts.description: null for a task without links.

invite_code.description: Its invite code; null for none.

held_count.description: Pending submissions the automatic checks held — decided by our team or our automatic check; you may also decide one.

open_to_all_at.description: When a team-first task opens to everyone (set at funding).

max_per_country.description: At most this many workers from any one country; null = no limit.

x_check.description: Each worker's X work is checked automatically.

x_check_fee_minor.description: What the X checks add to `fee_minor` for the task's places (0 without them).

x_check_price_micro.description: The X-check price per worker place in micro-dollars, frozen when the task was funded; null on a draft or without X checks.

employer_review.description: You approve this task's proofs (POST /submissions/{id}/approve) instead of our automatic review, until each proof's window passes.

disputes_open.description: Workers' disputes of a refusal still open on it (GET /disputes?task_id=…). Each keeps one place back until it is decided.

dedupe_keys.description: One person per item: workers who sent proof on, or hold a place on, another of your tasks sharing ANY of these keys cannot take this one. Empty for none.

order_ref.description: The order it belongs to (GET /orders/{ref}); null for none.

verify_url.description: Your own check: asked proof.check before a proof is stored, claim.check when a worker starts the task (with `verify_claims`), dispute.check when a dispute of your refusal reaches its deadline.

verify_secret.description: Present with `verify_url`: what signs our calls to it.

checker_note.description: Your private note for checking proofs; null for none. Only you and our staff see it — never a worker.

verify_claims.description: Workers who start it are asked about first (claim.check) — while a `verify_url` is set.

account.description: The verified account a worker must have, or null.

variations.description: Its groups of workers, in order — each with its places, pay and how many are taken and paid; empty for a task without them. `reward_minor` is the lowest group pay.

personal_links.description: Its links, one per worker, in order (given and not); empty for none. Workers never see this list: each sees only the link they hold.

personal_link_counts.description: null for a task without links.

invite_code.description: The invite code workers are shown with a Copy button; null for none.

notes.description: Your notes to the people working on it that are still up, newest first.

edited_at.description: When its words were last changed while it was live (POST /tasks/{id}/edit); null when never.

reports.description: GET /tasks/{id}: what workers reported about it that is still open, newest first (at most 10) — the reason and their words (links, addresses and names taken out, at most 300 characters), never who sent it.

LiveEditBody.description: Send only what changes. The kinds of proof, the money and who can take the task are not editable here.

instructions.description: The steps, one per line, as when the task was created.

proof_notes.description: One entry per proof requirement, in the order GET /tasks/{id} lists `proofs`: its new note, or null or "" to clear it. A list of another length answers 409 `proof_kinds_locked` with `count`.

step_index.description: The step (0-based) it belongs to; null = the task as a whole.

message.description: What to tell the people working on it about the change. Sent to them and posted as a note, with e-mail addresses and phone numbers hidden. Left out or blank: they are told the task was updated.

dedupe_key.description: Change or clear (null) the one-person-per-post key with the words, or alone. It takes effect at the next claim; nobody is told.

dedupe_keys.description: Or the whole list of keys (see TaskCreate), with the words or alone; null or [] clears them. Not with `dedupe_key`.

checker_note.description: Change or clear (null or "") your private note for checking proofs, with the words or alone. Alone, nobody is told and no version is kept: workers never see it. Our checker reads it from the next proof it looks at.

verify_claims.description: Ask before the start on or off, with the words or alone. true needs the task's `verify_url` (422 `verify_claims_needs_url`), checked before anything changes. It takes effect at the next start; nobody is told.

account.description: The verified account a worker must have, on or off (null), with the words or alone. It takes effect at the next start; a worker already on it is asked to prove one before sending proof.

personal_links.description: The task's links, one per worker, as you want them now — with the words or alone. A link already given to a worker stays whatever you send; the others follow the list. A task getting its first links needs one for every free place, and people already working on it get one each; a task that has links may not be left with fewer than before for its places (409 `personal_links_short` with `needed`) — adding some is always taken. Checked before anything changes.

invite_code.description: Set, change or clear (null) the invite code, with the words or alone. Alone it tells nobody.

dry_run.description: Run every check and answer what would happen; change nothing.

unchanged.description: Present (true) when nothing sent differs from the task as it is: nothing was written and nobody was told.

dry_run.description: Present (true) on a dry run: every check passed and nothing changed.

notified.description: How many people working on it were told — on a dry run, how many would be.

note.description: The note made from `message`, when one was sent.

body.description: As stored: e-mail addresses and phone numbers replaced by •••.

masked.description: Contact details were hidden before it was stored.

ResizeBody.description: At least one of `slots_total` and `reward_minor` — or, on a task with groups, `variations`.

slots_total.description: How many workers in all, paid and started included.

reward_minor.description: Pay per worker, in cents. Only up. On a task with groups: the lowest pay — every group paying less is raised to it.

variations.description: A task with groups: each group's places and pay, by its `id` (the others stay as they are) — instead of `slots_total` and `reward_minor`, never with them. On such a task a plain `slots_total` is shared among the groups by their places. 400 `variation_not_found`; 409 `reward_cannot_decrease` / `slots_below_taken` carry `variation_id`.

personal_links.description: A task with one link per worker: its links as you want them now, applied with the places in one change — more places need more links (409 `personal_links_short` with `needed`, a dry run too). A link already given to a worker stays whatever you send.

dry_run.description: Answer what would happen; change nothing.

changed.description: false when the numbers sent are the task's numbers already.

task.description: The task as the change leaves it (on a dry run: would leave it).

match_credit_returned_minor.description: Present when switch-offer match credit (microworker.app/migrate) was in the task: it goes back to your offer, not your balance.

extra_minor.description: Reserved from your available balance as part of the task's budget.

claims_raised.description: Workers who had started (not yet sent) and now get the new pay.

available_minor.description: Your available balance — now on a dry run, after the change otherwise.

funds_minor.description: What of your available balance can pay for jobs: money you added and credit, never money you earned.

enough.description: false when `extra_minor` is more than `funds_minor`: the real call would answer 402 (`insufficient_balance`, or `earnings_cannot_fund`).

variations.description: A task with groups: each group as the change leaves it (on a dry run: would leave it).

TaskVariationInput.description: One group of workers. `places` or `share_percent` — every group the same way.

label.description: What this group does, as workers see it: "Survey + 3 extra questions".

instruction.description: One line shown to this group above the common steps: "After the survey, answer the 3 extra questions."

share_percent.description: Percent of `slots_total`, turned into places at create (the largest remainder gets the odd place).

reward_minor.description: Pay per worker in this group, in cents. Defaults to the task's `reward_minor`.

slots_taken.description: Places in use in this group (started, waiting for review or paid).

places.description: At least the places in use in it.

SubmissionVariation.description: The group of the task this place is in; null on a task without groups.

PersonalLinkCounts.description: A task with one link per worker: `total` links, `assigned` (held by a worker now, or spent), `opened` (opened or copied by their worker — spent for good) and `left` (nobody holds them: what new workers can still get).

waiting.description: Proofs sent after the places were taken, waiting for one to open.

free_places.description: What a new worker can still take now: places − taken − open disputes − proofs waiting for a place (0 unless the task is open or paused).

held.description: Sent proofs our checks or review held for a decision.

disputes_open.description: Workers' disputes of a refusal on this task not decided yet — each keeps a place back.

TaskVisibility.description: Whether workers see the task on the board now, and why not.

moderation.description: `hidden`: it was live, then worker reports or a later look took it off the board. `in_review`: a person or our reviewer looks before it goes live (a first task, a flagged word, a kind only a plan may post).

reason.description: Why it is not on the board; null when it is.

paused_reason.description: While it is paused, why — the `reason` of the `task.paused` webhook (`reports`, `staff`, `link_not_working`, `proofs`, `region`, `review`, `employer`); null when it is not paused, or for a pause we cannot tell.

paused_by.description: While it is paused, who paused it: you (`employer`), our staff, or the platform by itself (`automatic`).

paused_at.description: While it is paused, when (ISO 8601, UTC).

paused_countries.description: While it is paused for `region`: the countries (ISO codes) workers found it not to work in. Resume it with PATCH /tasks/{id} `{ "action": "resume" }`; those countries stay closed to it.

c.description: What was found: copied_proof, reused_own_proof, example_image, blank_image, duplicate_file, tiny_image, unreadable_image, same_text, same_link, link_from_task, placeholder_text, too_fast (sent in `e` seconds; the task asks for `n`); on geo-tunnel tasks also tunnel_unused (the tunnel carried no real traffic for this claim), tunnel_wrong_country (`t` is the task's country, `seen` where the exit actually was) and tunnel_geo_split (`seen` lists the countries the geo vendors disagreed between). Since 2026-11-01 also, each holding the proof for a person: copied_comment (the comment matches a comment in another worker's earlier proof on this task, `ref` when it is on this task; `self` when the original is on the same screenshot), edited_image (saved by a photo editor; `ai` when made by an image generator), promo_picture (looks like an app-store promo picture), site_picture (the website's own preview picture); and placeholder_text with `src: 'screen'` is template text on a screenshot.

seed_covered.description: The paths in `screenshot_paths` where the platform covered the secret recovery words of a crypto wallet with a black box (the worker's private key — never kept). Absent when none.

verify_status.description: How the platform verified it by itself (a code, a Telegram join), if it did.

worker_country.description: The country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2) the worker started this task from; null when not known.

worker_device.description: The kind of device the proof was sent from (else the start): an Android phone, an iPhone, or a computer.

worker_joined_at.description: When the worker's account was made.

auto_approve_at.description: The end of its review window.

auto_pay_at.description: When it will be paid automatically; null when it will not be (held, decided, a conversion waiting for confirmation, or a task under staff review).

account.description: On a task that needs a verified account: the worker's account this place used — proved theirs by a code posted from it. null otherwise.

time_on_task_sec.description: Seconds between the worker first opening the task (or claiming it) and sending this.

in_team.description: The worker is one of your saved workers (the ones a `my_workers` task is for).

worker_approved.description: The worker's approved submissions across the platform.

worker_rejected.description: The worker's rejected submissions across the platform.

project_ids.description: Your projects (not archived) this worker is already in.

fix.description: A conversion task only: the fix you asked for, while it is open (else absent or null).

reversed_at.description: A conversion task only: when you took the pay back as not done.

click.description: A conversion task only: the worker's click code (mwc_…), so your server can find the submission of work it has not confirmed yet.

dispute.description: The worker's dispute of a refusal, if they opened one (one per proof): its `id` for GET /disputes and the decisions, its `status`, when it opened and when it is decided by itself if nobody decides it first (`decide_by`; null: a person decides).

worker_ref.description: The worker's id for your account (16 hex characters): the same for this worker on all your tasks, different for every other employer. `{worker}` written in your task's steps shows it to the worker, so a page of yours can tell who is coming.

updated_at.description: With paging only: when the submission last changed.

status.description: `resolved_worker`: the worker was paid; `resolved_employer`: the refusal stands; `closed_no_fault`: closed without pay — the worker could not have done it (not available in their country, a dead link), not counted against them.

reason.description: Why it was refused, as the worker was told.

by.description: `you`: you refused it (you decide first); `automatic`: our automatic review; `staff`: our staff.

worker_says.description: The worker's own words, as they wrote them.

decide_by.description: ISO UTC: when it is decided by itself if nobody decides it first — while it waits for our staff after our look (`staff_review`), the moment your refusal stands; null when a person decides however long it takes (or it is decided).

waiting_for.description: Who an open dispute waits for: `employer` — you (your own refusal, before `decide_by`); `staff` — our staff (a refusal they made, a reversal of paid work, a look that could not settle it, or `staff_review`); `automatic` — our automatic look (a refusal it made). null once decided. You can decide one of your own refusals whatever this says.

staff_review.description: Set while your refusal waits for our staff: at `decide_by` our look found the work done, you had given a reason, and your `verify_url` gave no clear answer to `dispute.check` (or the task has none). Nothing is paid unless you or our staff decide so; your refusal stands at the new `decide_by`.

since.description: ISO UTC: when it began waiting.

why.description: `employer_reason`: you gave a reason our look could not check.

automatic_look.description: What our automatic second look at the proof found, with the worker's words beside it; null before a look ran.

can_accept.description: You can pay the worker now (POST /disputes/{id}/accept).

can_uphold.description: You can keep your refusal now (POST /disputes/{id}/uphold).

can_send_back.description: You can let the worker send it again now (POST /disputes/{id}/send-back).

sent_back.description: The dispute was answered with one more try: the proof went back to its worker to send again (by you, or by our automatic look when it found something missing). Its `status` is `resolved_employer` — the proof as sent stays not accepted; what the worker sends next is checked like any proof and reaches you as a submission.

reward_minor.description: What the proof pays if it is decided for the worker.

duplicate.description: It was already decided this way; nothing changed.

paid_minor.description: What the worker was paid by this call (accept).

refunded_minor.description: On a task that has ended: what came back to you of what it kept for its disputes.

sent_back.description: send-back only: the proof went back to its worker for one more try.

fix.description: send-back only: what the worker reads (your note, else the refusal's own words) and until when they can send it again.

due_at.description: ISO UTC: the end of the time to fix it.

kind.description: `paid`: confirm it again before `due_at` or the pay is taken back; `unpaid`: nothing is paid until you confirm it.

held.description: Of those, the ones the automatic checks held.

OrderSkipped.description: A task of the order the action left alone — already past it (closed, or not open for a pause…).

resumed.description: POST /orders/{ref}/resume: the tasks back on the board.

active.description: It receives events: not switched off.

disabled_at.description: When it was switched off — by you (PATCH /webhooks/{id} `active: false`), or after 50 deliveries in a row failed. PATCH it with `active: true` to switch it on again.

disabled_reason.description: `paused`: you switched it off. `failing`: 50 deliveries in a row failed.

secret.description: whsec_… — shown only in this answer.

WebhookEvent.description: The body of every webhook request. Verify the Microworker-Signature header before trusting it: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<raw body>" keyed with your endpoint secret>; reject a t more than five minutes old. Microworker-Event-Id is the same on every retry of one event.

type.description: `task.moderation_changed`: one of your tasks went into a review, was hidden, approved or declined, or came back on the board by itself (`data`: `task_id`, `moderation`, `reason`, `reports`). `task.board_kind_changed`: where the board lists one of your tasks changed (`data`: `task_id`, `board_kind`, `was`). `task.paused` / `task.resumed`: one of your tasks stopped or started running, why, who and when (`data`: `task_id`, `status`, `reason`, `by`, `at`, and for a pause `reports` + `report_texts` or `countries`). `dispute.opened` / `dispute.decided`: a worker disputed a refusal of their proof, and how it ended.

worker_ref.description: The worker's id for your account, as on GET /tasks/{id}/submissions.

click.description: The worker's click code on a postback task.

revisions.description: How many times this proof was sent back for a fix — 0 for a first proof. A proof sent again after a fix comes back on the SAME id with `submission.created` again and `revisions` ≥ 1: decide it like a new one.

account.description: On a task that needs a verified account: the worker's account this place used. null otherwise.

auto_pay_at.description: When it is paid automatically if nobody decides it first (as on GET /submissions); null when it will not be. A proof paid that way has status `auto_approved` — count it with the approved ones.

status.description: `task.paused` / `task.resumed`: its status now — as `status` on GET /tasks/{id}.

moderation.description: `task.moderation_changed`: `hidden` (taken off the board), `in_review` (looked at before it goes live), `shown` (on the board, again), `declined` (taken down; its money came back).

reason.description: `task.moderation_changed`: why — worker reports, a review, our staff, or `automatic`: hidden by worker reports, it came back by itself (they stay open for our staff, who may still decide them). `task.paused`: `reports` (workers reported that it does not work), `staff` (our staff paused it, or found that it does not work), `link_not_working` (our link check found its link dead or parked), `proofs` (workers' proofs show it cannot be done), `region` (its site or app is not available in the countries it is offered in), `review` (a later look wants a person first — `task.moderation_changed` comes too), `employer` (you paused it). `task.resumed`: `automatic` (paused by worker reports, it came back by itself: other workers were paid for it after those reports, so they no longer count), `staff`, `employer` (you). The same word is `visibility.paused_reason` on GET /tasks/{id} while it is paused.

reports.description: `task.moderation_changed` and `task.paused` with `reason: "reports"`: how many reports counted.

report_texts.description: `task.paused` with `reason: "reports"`: what the reports that paused it said (up to three, newest first; contact details hidden; never who wrote them). Empty when they were made without words.

countries.description: `task.paused` with `reason: "region"`: the countries (ISO codes) workers found it not to work in.

by.description: `task.paused`: who paused it — you, our staff, or the platform by itself.

at.description: `task.paused` / `task.resumed`: when (ISO 8601, UTC). Resume a paused task with PATCH /tasks/{id} `{ "action": "resume" }`.

board_kind.description: `task.board_kind_changed`: where the board lists it now — as `board_kind` on GET /tasks/{id}.

click.description: The mw_click code from the worker's personal link (mwc_…).

reference.description: Your own id for the conversion, kept with it for your records.

status.description: `auto_approved`: paid. `held`: our account checks held it — a person decides, nothing was paid. `confirmed`: recorded, paid when the checks finish (`checking`).

already.description: This code was already paid; nothing more was paid.

fix.description: This call confirmed a fix you had asked for on paid work: the pay stays.

target_devices.description: A device limit: iPhones only, computers only (Windows or Mac only too), or both, pay more.

audience.description: `my_workers` and `project` price a task for a small group you chose.

model.description: Which version of the guide answered.

raise_minor.description: A higher price to offer: half again over the recommendation (at least a cent more), never past high_minor.

confidence.description: `low` when the posting did not say what kind of work it is.
